question: As a nurse, what is the best approach when checking thyroid lab results for a pregnant patient?

options.A: Ignoring the thyroid panel since hormones do not affect the gland
options.B: Immediately starting the patient on synthetic thyroid replacement
options.C: Using pregnancy-specific reference ranges instead of standard charts
options.D: Repeating the blood draw because the results are always inaccurate

explanation: Brilliant! Since a pregnant woman's baseline chemistry changes, you always want to use specialized pregnancy reference charts to read her labs correctly. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h7)

question: Which facility represents the primary level of mental health care in Nigeria?

options.A: University teaching hospitals
options.B: Local government health clinics and posts
options.C: State-owned general hospitals
options.D: Federal neuropsychiatric hospitals

explanation: Primary care is right at the grassroots level—the local health posts and clinics closest to our communities. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: What does a nurse check when assessing normal uterine involution during a postnatal home visit?

options.A: The complete absence of lochia discharge after twenty-four hours
options.B: The permanent softening of the abdominal wall muscles
options.C: The gradual decrease in the size and height of the uterus
options.D: The rapid increase in maternal body weight

explanation: Involution is the normal process where the uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy size, felt as a steadily lowering fundal height. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why are family planning supply methods so important for community reproductive health?

options.A: They give clients direct control over family spacing and reduce unintended pregnancies
options.B: They are always 100 percent effective regardless of how they are used
options.C: They require no client education or counseling from healthcare workers
options.D: They completely eliminate all risks of sexually transmitted infections globally

explanation: By putting easy-to-use options straight into people's hands, communities can better plan family sizes and stay healthier. Great job! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h1)

question: A nurse checks daily blood glucose numbers sent automatically from a patient's smart glucometer at home. What is this called?

options.A: Electronic health record archiving
options.B: Store-and-forward imaging
options.C: Remote patient monitoring
options.D: Synchronous tele-surgery

explanation: Great job! Remote patient monitoring uses connected home devices to keep an eye on vital signs without the patient needing to visit the clinic. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h2)

question: When you face sudden stress, what is the very first stage of the General Adaptation Syndrome?

options.A: Stage of exhaustion
options.B: Homeostatic recovery
options.C: Alarm reaction
options.D: Stage of resistance

explanation: That's right! The alarm reaction is your classic 'fight-or-flight' moment where adrenaline kicks in and gets your body ready for quick action. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the main goal of nursing inquiry?

options.A: To systematically search for knowledge relevant to practice
options.B: To write hospital policies without clinical input
options.C: To punish nurses who make clinical mistakes
options.D: To reduce the number of hospital admissions

explanation: Nursing inquiry is all about finding reliable knowledge to improve how we care for patients, teach, and run hospitals. You'll see this come up often in practice! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h1)

question: A patient just had cataract surgery and is getting ready to go home. What is a key instruction to give them?

options.A: Wash your face vigorously with antibacterial soap daily
options.B: Sleep flat on your back without using any pillows
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and straining during bowel movements
options.D: Keep the affected eye uncovered at all times

explanation: Spot on! Straining or heavy lifting ramps up the pressure inside the eye, which is the last thing you want right after eye surgery. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the medical term for pale, bulky, foul-smelling stools caused by unabsorbed dietary fat?

options.A: Steatorrhea
options.B: Hematuria
options.C: Proteinuria
options.D: Glycosuria

explanation: Spot on! Steatorrhea is the clinical term for fatty stools that happen when the body fails to absorb lipids properly. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h5)

question: Which type of bougie uses heavy mercury or tungsten fillings so gravity helps it slide down?

options.A: Rigid urethral sounds
options.B: Eder-Puestow metal springs
options.C: Hurst or Maloney bougies
options.D: Pneumatic balloon dilators

explanation: Hurst and Maloney bougies have heavy tips filled with things like mercury or tungsten. This extra weight lets gravity help guide them smoothly down the esophagus. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h2)

question: Why do many newly diagnosed patients choose to isolate themselves socially?

options.A: Physical inability to leave the bed
options.B: Strict medical orders to stay home
options.C: Fear of social rejection and stigma
options.D: Loss of interest in human interaction

explanation: Worries about how family, friends, and employers might react drive many patients to hide their status and pull away from support networks. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h1)

question: Why is immediacy important when applying the Hot Stove Rule?

options.A: It allows the manager to go home earlier
options.B: It connects the consequence directly to the rule violation
options.C: It prevents other staff members from noticing the error
options.D: It gives the nurse less time to defend themselves

explanation: Acting quickly ensures the employee clearly links the disciplinary action to their specific misbehavior. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h3)

question: At what point during your shift should you separate (segregate) hospital waste?

options.A: Right at the exact time and place you create it
options.B: After the cleaning staff pack the bins
options.C: When the waste reaches the hospital incinerator
options.D: During weekly environmental health inspections

explanation: Always sort your waste immediately as you generate it! Waiting until later leads to mistakes and accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is a major goal of family planning within Primary Health Care?

options.A: Helping parents properly space their children for better health
options.B: Controlling the exact height of newborn babies
options.C: Ensuring families only have male children
options.D: Completely banning families from having children

explanation: Family planning allows mothers to regain their health between pregnancies and ensures better care for existing children. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why are grab bars installed in bathrooms for individuals with physical disabilities?

options.A: To block water from splashing onto the bathroom floor tiles
options.B: To hold towels and washcloths within easy reach of the bathing area
options.C: To serve as hanging storage for lightweight assistive devices
options.D: To provide stable support during transfers on and off the toilet or in the shower

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces combined with transfers make grab bars essential safety features for preventing falls. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is considered a direct cause of maternal death?

options.A: Sickle cell anemia
options.B: Eclampsia
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Eclampsia (severe pregnancy-induced high blood pressure leading to seizures) is a direct complication of pregnancy. The others are medical conditions made worse by pregnancy (indirect). [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h3)

question: An elderly patient refuses to eat because their dentures hurt their gums. What should you recommend as a nurse?

options.A: Stop all nutritional assessments and wait for natural recovery.
options.B: Prescribe an expensive vitamin supplement over the phone.
options.C: Insist that the patient eat hard raw vegetables immediately.
options.D: Recommend soft, nutrient-dense foods and refer for dental care.

explanation: You nailed it! Soft foods keep them nourished without pain, while a dental visit fixes the root cause of the problem. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)?

options.A: To force every patient to visit the hospital daily
options.B: To track patient vital signs from their home using digital devices
options.C: To store paper records in a warehouse far from the clinic
options.D: To replace human nurses with automated computer screens

explanation: RPM sends real-time health data like blood pressure or sugar levels from the patient's house straight to the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is keeping our core body temperature within a steady, normal range so important?

options.A: To keep the skeletal muscles from contracting too quickly
options.B: To prevent the bones from becoming brittle over time
options.C: To support normal metabolic processes and cellular function
options.D: To ensure the digestive system absorbs enough water

explanation: Spot on! Our body's chemical reactions and tiny cellular engines need a stable temperature to run smoothly without breaking down. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is high out-of-pocket spending dangerous for ordinary citizens?

options.A: It makes doctors prescribe too many generic medications
options.B: It lowers the total number of registered nurses
options.C: It forces families into financial ruin during sudden illness
options.D: It prevents the government from collecting any taxes

explanation: When patients must pay directly out of pocket for every service, medical bills can easily drain family savings and cause poverty. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a rehabilitation hospital?

options.A: Restoring lost function and maximizing independence
options.B: Treating acute infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: Stabilizing immediate life-threatening organ failure
options.D: Providing long-term terminal palliative care

explanation: You got this! Rehab hospitals help patients rebuild their strength and everyday skills after major life changes, rather than managing sudden medical emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is the main cause of neonatal tetanus in newborn babies?

options.A: Mother-to-child transmission across the placenta during birth
options.B: Unhygienic practices during umbilical cord cutting and care
options.C: Inhalation of airborne bacterial droplets from coughing adults
options.D: Consuming unpasteurized milk during the first week of life

explanation: Correct! Neonatal tetanus happens when tetanus germs get into the unhealed umbilical stump, often due to unsterilized instruments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h4)

question: How do advanced medical technologies generally impact healthcare supply?

options.A: They can improve efficiency and expand diagnostic capabilities
options.B: They automatically decrease the number of patients seeking care
options.C: They always reduce the total cost of operating a hospital ward
options.D: They eliminate the need for skilled nursing staff completely

explanation: Spot on! New tech helps hospitals run smoother and test patients faster, boosting what the facility can handle. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why should you, as a nurse, look beyond just the sick patient and check on the whole household?

options.A: Patients never feel stressed if medical staff are around
options.B: Nurses are legally required to counsel all relatives
options.C: When one person gets sick, it stresses everyone else out too
options.D: Hospital rules say family members must pay all bills directly

explanation: Illness doesn't happen in a vacuum. When a family member falls sick, it creates a ripple effect of worry and stress for everyone close to them. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why should you suction a patient's breathing tube based on clinical need rather than a strict routine schedule?

options.A: Suctioning can cause mucosal trauma, bleeding, and oxygen desaturation
options.B: Mucus production completely stops once a patient is intubated
options.C: Strict schedules increase the cost of disposable suction catheters
options.D: Scheduled suctioning causes the ventilator to malfunction

explanation: Suctioning is rough on the delicate lining of the windpipe and temporarily steals oxygen. We only do it when we actually hear or see secretions, protecting our patient from unnecessary harm. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why do student nurses need to know where pharmaceutical drugs come from?

options.A: To appreciate why precise dosages and chemical standardization matter
options.B: So they can manufacture the medications directly in the hospital ward
options.C: To replace traditional healers in local communities effectively
options.D: Because plant-based drugs never interact with synthetic lab drugs

explanation: Understanding drug origins helps you see why exact dosing is so vital for patient safety on the ward. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h1)

question: What action should a nurse take immediately before leaving a computer workstation on the ward?

options.A: Lock or log out of the workstation to prevent unauthorized access
options.B: Minimize the patient charts without locking the screen
options.C: Turn off the main electrical power switch in the room
options.D: Leave the screen open for the next shift nurse

explanation: Locking unattended screens prevents unauthorized people from viewing confidential patient health records. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary driving factor behind gender-based violence in most societies?

options.A: Sudden economic inflation within households
options.B: A lack of religious devotion in the community
options.C: Unequal power relations and patriarchal norms
options.D: Genetic predispositions toward aggressive behavior

explanation: GBV is deeply driven by structural inequalities and cultural beliefs that promote dominance and control over specific genders. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why do nursing students still need to learn traditional medication abbreviations?

options.A: Older paper charts and verbal orders still use them
options.B: Hospitals legally require staff to write in Latin shorthand
options.C: Computers cannot process plain English medication names
options.D: Using abbreviations prevents all forms of medical errors

explanation: Spot on! Even though things are modernizing, you'll still see these shorthand terms on older paper notes and hear experienced clinicians use them on the ward. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which antibody class is mostly found in body secretions like breast milk and saliva?

options.A: IgD
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgA
options.D: IgE

explanation: Secretory IgA is our body's frontline defender in wet areas! It guards mucosal linings in our respiratory and digestive tracts, and is proudly passed to babies through breast milk. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h3)

question: What does interoperability mean in healthcare technology?

options.A: Patients can update their own charts without a clinician
options.B: Every hospital uses a completely different brand of computer
options.C: Doctors and nurses work separate shifts without communicating
options.D: Different health systems can share data seamlessly

explanation: Interoperability allows separate computer networks and hospitals to talk to each other and exchange patient records safely. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between an antiseptic and a disinfectant?

options.A: Antiseptics are heated before use, while disinfectants are kept at room temperature.
options.B: Antiseptics are used on living tissue, while disinfectants are used on inanimate surfaces.
options.C: Disinfectants are safe to drink, while antiseptics are strictly for external wounds.
options.D: Disinfectants kill viruses, while antiseptics only kill bacteria and fungi.

explanation: Antiseptics are formulated to be safe enough for human skin and wounds, whereas disinfectants are harsh chemicals meant only for objects and furniture. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h1)

question: Which type of safety intervention is generally considered the most effective at preventing future errors?

options.A: Holding a 10-minute verbal lecture during morning shift handover
options.B: Strong system changes like automated hard-stops or redesigning equipment layouts
options.C: Asking staff to memorize a new policy document binder
options.D: Sending out a mandatory email warning staff to be more careful

explanation: Forced functions and system redesigns rely on technology or environment rather than human memory, making them much more reliable. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h8)

question: What should be clearly recorded in the patient's register when a standing order is used?

options.A: The specific protocol used, assessment findings, and treatments given
options.B: The political affiliation of the patient receiving care
options.C: The personal home address of the facility's medical director
options.D: A detailed financial profit statement for the pharmacy unit

explanation: Proper documentation requires noting the exact protocol followed, clinical findings, and interventions administered for legal and continuity purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h7)

question: What shape is the anterior (front) fontanelle?

options.A: Round-shaped
options.B: Diamond-shaped
options.C: Oval-shaped
options.D: Triangle-shaped

explanation: You got it! The anterior fontanelle sits right at the front and is famously diamond-shaped. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T12#GNS121_U6_T12_h2)

question: What is the main foundation of public health when looking at nutrition?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic use
options.B: Regular surgical screening
options.C: Adequate nutrition
options.D: Frequent vaccination

explanation: Great job! Eating proper food gives the body the energy it needs to stay healthy and fight off sickness, which is why it forms the bedrock of public health. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h1)

question: What does internal validity measure in an experimental study?

options.A: Whether the study can be used in every hospital worldwide
options.B: How many nurses were hired to assist with data collection
options.C: Whether the treatment truly caused the observed outcome
options.D: How fast the patients answered the survey questions

explanation: Internal validity checks if outside factors ruined the experiment, ensuring the intervention itself made the difference. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is it usually a mistake to jump straight into psychological counseling before sorting out a patient's Tier 1 needs?

options.A: Specialized medications will work twice as fast
options.B: The client will automatically recover without needing shelter
options.C: The psychological interventions will likely fail because survival anxiety overrides therapy
options.D: Counseling becomes much more effective because the client focuses inward

explanation: It makes total sense: if a patient is freezing, starving, or scared for their physical life, they cannot focus on talking through emotional trauma. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is a major drawback or limitation of using research checklists?

options.A: They cost more money than any other research tool
options.B: They are completely impossible to analyze statistically
options.C: They take months of training to read and write
options.D: They can oversimplify complex clinical situations

explanation: Checklists are great, but ticking boxes can sometimes strip away the rich details of a complex clinical scenario. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h7)

question: Which sign is most characteristic of a tension pneumothorax?

options.A: Frequent coughing with clear, thin mucus production
options.B: A slow and steady heart rate with warm, dry skin
options.C: Absent breath sounds on the affected side of the chest
options.D: Equal and bilateral chest expansion during breathing

explanation: Trapped air collapses the lung and prevents air entry, resulting in absent or significantly diminished breath sounds on that side. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the normal adult reference range for white blood cells?

options.A: 4,500 to 11,000 per microliter
options.B: 10 to 14 grams per deciliter
options.C: 4.2 to 5.4 million per microliter
options.D: 150,000 to 450,000 per microliter

explanation: A healthy adult usually has between 4,500 and 11,000 white blood cells per microliter. Think of this as your body's standing army ready to fight infection! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why are run charts particularly useful for busy clinical nursing units?

options.A: They require very little statistical training to read
options.B: They replace the need for writing patient care notes
options.C: They automatically dispense patient medications safely
options.D: They permanently eliminate all hospital infections

explanation: Because they are simple and visual, clinical staff can easily interpret them without needing advanced statistical skills. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h1)

question: When doing a quick ABCDE emergency check on a patient, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coughing
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Consciousness
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: A is Airway, B is Breathing, and C is Circulation! You check pulses and bleeding here. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of mitigation in disaster management?

options.A: To provide immediate medical care during a crisis
options.B: To reduce the severity of potential hazards
options.C: To conduct evacuation drills right before a storm
options.D: To rebuild homes after a disaster has occurred

explanation: Mitigation is all about taking action *before* a disaster strikes to lessen its blow on people and property. Think of it as putting up strong safeguards early! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders when promoting girl child education?

options.A: They work exclusively as classroom teachers in secondary boarding schools
options.B: They hold immense influence over local cultural norms and community acceptance
options.C: They are responsible for funding all primary health care clinics in rural areas
options.D: They write the national school curriculum and select all textbook titles

explanation: That's correct! Because local and religious leaders guide community beliefs, having their support makes it much easier to change attitudes and help girls stay in school. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h6)

question: Why do vaguely worded living wills cause problems for the healthcare team?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to read handwritten documents
options.B: Because insurance companies refuse to pay for vague medical forms
options.C: Because hospitals require notarized stamps on every single page
options.D: Because terms like 'heroic measures' can mean different things to different people

explanation: Vague phrases create ambiguity, leaving nurses and physicians unsure of whether the patient intended to refuse specific interventions like intubation or IV fluids. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: What does a 'feasible' research project mean for a student?

options.A: Whether the hospital will change its name after the study
options.B: Whether the research topic is popular on social media
options.C: How many international awards the study might win
options.D: Whether the study can actually be done with available resources

explanation: Feasibility is just about being realistic—making sure you have enough time, money, and materials to finish the study without burning out. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h3)

question: How should community mental health nurses best approach traditional healers?

options.A: Through respectful dialogue and collaborative education
options.B: By threatening them with immediate police arrest
options.C: By ignoring their presence in the local community
options.D: By adopting all of their religious rituals into the hospital

explanation: Wonderful approach! Working alongside healers with mutual respect builds trust, making them much more likely to refer patients safely to formal hospitals. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h7)

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a nurse working in community health?

options.A: It prevents patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.B: It allows the nurse to bypass standard medical protocols safely
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives financial awards from village chiefs
options.D: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build genuine trust

explanation: Spot on! Cultural humility means approaching people with an open, respectful mind, honoring their traditions while gently sharing health knowledge. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is it so important to keep the initial scope of a test of change very small?

options.A: It prevents overwhelming staff and keeps potential disruption to a minimum
options.B: It guarantees that no data will ever be lost during the shift
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever expand the project later on
options.D: It satisfies legal requirements for experimental medical research

explanation: Keeping things tiny means your team won't get stressed out, and if the idea flops, nobody gets hurt and patient care stays safe. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h4)

question: What happens to the fetal skull bones after the baby is delivered and moulding is no longer needed?

options.A: They remain permanently overlapped until the child reaches toddler age
options.B: They fuse together immediately to protect the brain from outside injury
options.C: They gradually return to their normal shape as the pressure is relieved
options.D: They separate permanently and require surgical correction in the nursery

explanation: Because the skull bones are flexible and joined by elastic tissue, the head regains its normal rounded appearance shortly after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h2)

question: A resident needs daily sterile dressing changes for a deep surgical wound. Which facility type is best suited for this care?

options.A: An adult day care center
options.B: A skilled nursing facility
options.C: A standard retirement community
options.D: An independent living apartment

explanation: Complex sterile wound care requires the expert clinical hands and continuous monitoring found in a skilled nursing facility. Spot on! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way to prevent violence in our communities?

options.A: Challenging harmful cultural norms
options.B: Establishing strong legal referral networks
options.C: Promoting rigid gender stereotypes
options.D: Educating youth on healthy relationships

explanation: Well spotted! We want to break down harmful stereotypes, not promote them, to help keep communities safe. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h6)

question: Which specific cell type is the main building block found inside a chronic granuloma?

options.A: Platelet
options.B: Macrophage
options.C: Neutrophil
options.D: Erythrocyte

explanation: Macrophages are the star players here! They morph into special shapes to form the core of every granuloma. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h5)

question: How does cerebrospinal fluid protect the brain from injury?

options.A: By providing buoyancy that reduces the net weight of the brain
options.B: By locking the brain rigidly in place to prevent all movement
options.C: By generating electrical currents that power nerve conduction
options.D: By inflating the skull bones to create a larger cranial vault

explanation: You got it! Floating in this fluid makes the heavy brain feel much lighter, keeping delicate tissue safe from being crushed by its own weight against the skull. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to improve teamwork communication?

options.A: Encouraging staff to speak up immediately about safety concerns
options.B: Maintaining strict professional hierarchies that discourage questions
options.C: Using closed-loop communication by repeating back instructions
options.D: Applying standardized handover tools during shift changes

explanation: Spot on! Rigid 'don't question senior staff' attitudes are dangerous because they stop junior nurses from speaking up when they spot a safety issue. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why is patient coercion a serious worry during research recruitment?

options.A: Ethical boards do not allow patients to receive free medication
options.B: Coerced patients always give false answers on questionnaires
options.C: Patients might feel forced to join because their nurse or doctor asked
options.D: Hospital management requires a 100 percent recruitment rate

explanation: Brilliant! Patients respect their nurses and doctors so much that they might fear getting bad care if they say 'no,' which makes true voluntary consent tricky. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h7)

question: What generally happens to the tracheostomy hole (stoma) after the tube is permanently removed?

options.A: It requires major plastic surgery to sew shut
options.B: It naturally heals closed with a simple dressing
options.C: It must be plugged with a permanent metal cap
options.D: It remains permanently open for air passage

explanation: Nature is amazing! Covered with a simple dressing, the stoma usually shrinks and closes up on its own within a few days. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is the correct action to take if a sterile syringe needle accidentally brushes against the outside of the nurse's clean uniform?

options.A: Use the needle anyway since the uniform was freshly laundered
options.B: Discard the needle and syringe immediately and get new ones
options.C: Wipe the needle with an alcohol swab and continue using it
options.D: Dip the needle into boiling water for ten seconds before use

explanation: Uniforms are not sterile. Any contact with non-sterile surfaces contaminates the equipment, requiring immediate replacement to prevent infection. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h4)

question: What does open disclosure involve following a medical error?

options.A: Communicating transparently and empathetically with the patient and family about what happened
options.B: Sending a written letter through the mail without offering a meeting
options.C: Blaming the pharmacy department publicly during morning ward rounds
options.D: Hiding the mistake from the family until legal counsel advises otherwise

explanation: Open disclosure means being honest, clear, and empathetic with patients and families when medical errors occur. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which lab tests are most important when starting a patient on an antipsychotic known for metabolic side effects?

options.A: Direct measurement of brain wave activity
options.B: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
options.C: Routine throat swab for bacterial culture
options.D: Complete stool analysis for parasites

explanation: Correct! Because these drugs can disrupt blood sugar and fats, keeping an eye on glucose and lipid levels is essential. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: Which option best describes a holistic psychiatric care plan?

options.A: Combining medical treatment with lifestyle and complementary interventions
options.B: Treating mental illness only through strict physical isolation
options.C: Relying solely on herbal remedies while avoiding all prescription drugs
options.D: Focusing exclusively on physical vital signs during hospitalization

explanation: Holistic care looks at the whole human being—blending modern medicine with healthy lifestyle choices and supportive therapies. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h6)

question: A clinic manager wants to know the most common uniform size ordered by new staff. Which measure should she use?

options.A: Mean
options.B: Mode
options.C: Median
options.D: Range

explanation: Uniform sizes are categories rather than math numbers, so the mode helps us find the most frequent size ordered. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T4#GNS217_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to design a mental health program without conducting a prior needs assessment?

options.A: The program might waste resources on problems the community does not actually face
options.B: Patients will immediately reject any free medication offered
options.C: Doctors will go on strike if they are not consulted first
options.D: The ministry of health will refuse to print flyers for the event

explanation: Without assessing real needs, health workers risk imposing foreign or irrelevant solutions that fail to address what the community truly struggles with. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h4)

question: When an artificial intelligence alert pops up on a patient monitor, what should the nurse do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately based on the computer screen
options.B: Ignore the patient completely because the computer is always right
options.C: Turn off all hospital monitors so they stop making noise
options.D: Evaluate the alert and use clinical judgment to decide the next step

explanation: Technology is a support tool, and nurses must always apply their own professional assessment before taking action. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the defining feature of a Cost-Benefit Analysis in healthcare?

options.A: Outcomes are measured strictly in natural clinical units like blood pressure
options.B: Both costs and health outcomes are measured in monetary terms
options.C: It completely ignores financial expenses to focus on patient emotions
options.D: It is only used when two treatments produce identical results

explanation: In a Cost-Benefit Analysis, even the health outcomes are converted into money (like naira). This lets you directly compare cash spent to cash saved or earned. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is 'closed-loop communication' so important during a chaotic resuscitation?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from having to touch the patient
options.B: It confirms that instructions given by the team leader are clearly heard and executed
options.C: It ensures that family members outside the room stay quiet
options.D: It reduces the need for documentation after the code is over

explanation: Brilliant! Repeating instructions back (like 'Giving 1mg epinephrine now') stops dangerous mistakes when things get loud and fast. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h6)

question: When cleaning the mother's perineal area before delivery, why must you always wipe from front to back?

options.A: To stimulate uterine contractions and speed up the second stage
options.B: To ensure that the antiseptic solution reaches deep into the cervix
options.C: To prevent the transfer of fecal bacteria into the vagina and urethra
options.D: To make the perineal skin stretch more easily during crowning

explanation: Wiping front-to-back keeps nasty E. coli from the rectal area away from the birth canal, preventing nasty postpartum infections. Simple rule, big impact! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h4)

question: What is the most effective way for a nurse to communicate health education in a rural Nigerian community?

options.A: Writing long formal research papers
options.B: Using simple local languages and clear pictures
options.C: Handing out advanced medical textbooks
options.D: Speaking only in technical medical English

explanation: To ensure understanding, health education must be delivered in a language and format that everyday community members easily grasp. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a key ethical duty of a nurse regarding alternative therapies?

options.A: Selling approved herbal supplements directly to hospital patients
options.B: Refusing to care for patients who use meditation
options.C: Protecting patients from potential harm and financial exploitation
options.D: Guaranteeing that every alternative remedy will cure mental illness

explanation: As patient advocates, nurses protect clients from unsafe substances and make sure they aren't taken advantage of by fake miracle cures. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is the most crucial piece of history to gather first when assessing an animal bite?

options.A: The exact weight and age of the bitted patient
options.B: The color and breed of the animal involved
options.C: The insurance and home address of the owner
options.D: The exact time of the bite and tetanus status

explanation: Timing tells us about infection risks, while checking the patient's tetanus status lets us know if a booster shot is urgently needed. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of these patients is most at risk of catching a hospital infection?

options.A: A middle-aged nurse working full-time in the surgical ward
options.B: A healthy outpatient visiting the clinic for a routine checkup
options.C: A young adult recovering from a simple sprained ankle
options.D: An elderly patient receiving chemotherapy and using a urinary catheter

explanation: Exactly. Between age, chemotherapy lowering their immunity, and a catheter creating an easy entry path, this patient's defenses are stretched thin. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h6)

question: How many links make up the standard chain of infection?

options.A: Ten links
options.B: Six links
options.C: Four links
options.D: Eight links

explanation: You've got this! The chain of infection is made up of six links, starting from the infectious agent all the way to the susceptible host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason for drawing a process map during a quality project?

options.A: To diagnose complex medical conditions in emergency room patients
options.B: To punish nurses who fail to complete their documentation on time
options.C: To calculate the exact financial budget required for a new ward
options.D: To visualize every step of a workflow and identify hidden bottlenecks

explanation: A process map lays out each step of a task so your team can easily spot where delays or frustrations happen. [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h4)

question: If someone suffers from lead poisoning, what type of epidemiological agent is at fault?

options.A: A biological agent
options.B: A nutritional agent
options.C: A physical agent
options.D: A chemical agent

explanation: Poisons, toxins, and heavy metals are chemical agents because they cause harm through chemical reactions in the body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h3)

question: Which computer system is strong enough to host an entire hospital's electronic health record database?

options.A: Pocket smartphone
options.B: Mainframe computer
options.C: Personal desktop
options.D: Analog signal monitor

explanation: That's right! Mainframes have the immense power needed to keep a whole hospital's database running smoothly and securely. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: In nursing research, what do we mean by the word 'population'?

options.A: Every person living in the city where the study takes place
options.B: The specific patients who dropped out of a clinical trial
options.C: The entire group of people the researcher wants to study
options.D: Only the nurses working in a specific hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! In research, the 'population' is just the big group of people you are curious about and want to learn more from. Think of it as the big picture before you zoom in. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why do animal hookworm larvae cause wandering red lines on human skin instead of a deeper infection?

options.A: Because humans are accidental dead-end hosts where the larvae cannot complete their life cycle
options.B: Because topical soaps paralyze the nervous system of the parasites immediately
options.C: Because human white blood cells instantly freeze the larvae in place under the skin
options.D: Because the larvae lack the physical strength to bite through muscle fascia

explanation: Since humans aren't their normal hosts, the larvae get confused and wander aimlessly in the top layers of the skin. Makes sense when you picture it! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h3)

question: A nurse needs to verify a complex intravenous drug dose quickly before administration. What is the best way to use mobile technology here?

options.A: Use a verified clinical app on a smartphone to double-check the calculation
options.B: Guess the dosage based on how big the patient looks
options.C: Skip the medication entirely if it looks complicated
options.D: Ask another patient in the ward what dose they received

explanation: Mobile reference tools help nurses confirm safe medication dosages instantly at the point of care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h3)

question: When severe anxiety kicks off the 'fight-or-flight' response, which physical sign do you expect to see?

options.A: Constricted pupils
options.B: Slowed digestion with increased salivation
options.C: Decreased respiratory rate
options.D: Increased heart rate (tachycardia)

explanation: You got it! Adrenaline pumps through the body, making the heart beat fast and hard to get us ready to run or fight. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h4)

question: What does 'cultural humility' look like in everyday nursing practice?

options.A: Insisting that modern medicine always supersedes client beliefs
options.B: Apologizing to the client for every medical diagnosis given
options.C: Avoiding all conversations about culture to prevent discomfort
options.D: Viewing oneself as a learner eager to understand the client's worldview

explanation: You nailed it! Cultural humility means dropping the expert badge and being genuinely curious to learn about the patient's life straight from them. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which scenario represents a violation of the 'right time' medication principle?

options.A: Crushing a simple uncoated tablet for a patient who cannot swallow pills
options.B: Giving a routine morning antibiotic two hours late without a valid reason
options.C: Documenting the medication immediately after the patient swallows it
options.D: Checking the patient's identification band before opening the package

explanation: Administering medications significantly outside their scheduled time frame can cause blood levels to drop too low or spike too high. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main clinical advantage of giving asthma medication through an inhaler instead of a pill?

options.A: It completely avoids the need for any patient breathing coordination
options.B: It provides a much longer drug duration lasting up to a week
options.C: It prevents the drug from ever entering the patient's bloodstream
options.D: It delivers the drug directly to the airways for rapid local action

explanation: Inhalers send the medication straight to the lungs where it's needed most. This brings quick relief with smaller doses than taking a pill by mouth. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which set of clinical signs points directly to neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)?

options.A: High fever, extreme muscle rigidity, and unstable vitals
options.B: Uncontrolled euphoria and excessive talkativeness
options.C: Hyperactive bowel sounds and sudden weight loss
options.D: Slurred speech, itchy skin rash, and low fever

explanation: Think of NMS as a dangerous fire in the body: extremely high fever, muscles stiff as boards (lead-pipe rigidity), and wild swings in blood pressure and heart rate. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is the standard temperature inside a clinical incubator for growing human pathogens?

options.A: 80 to 90 degrees Celsius
options.B: 35 to 37 degrees Celsius
options.C: 10 to 15 degrees Celsius
options.D: 50 to 60 degrees Celsius

explanation: Think about normal body temperature! Since these germs live inside human hosts, the incubator is set right around 37°C to make them feel right at home. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h3)

question: You are talking to a patient with profound hearing loss. What is the very first thing you should do to help them understand you?

options.A: Rely entirely on telephone calls for follow-up
options.B: Face the patient directly and ensure good lighting
options.C: Turn on the television to keep the room comfortable
options.D: Speak in a very loud voice from across the room

explanation: Always face your patient and make sure the room is well-lit so they can read your lips and pick up on your facial expressions. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T14#GNS324_U4_T14_h6)

question: What do we mean by 'psychological safety' in a nursing unit?

options.A: The mandatory wearing of protective equipment
options.B: The physical security of staff against outside intruders
options.C: The freedom to speak up about safety concerns without fear
options.D: The absence of stressful patients in the ward

explanation: Exactly! Psychological safety means you can ask questions or report a worry without stressing about being yelled at or victimized by colleagues. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h3)

question: What does evaluating a menu mean in quality improvement?

options.A: A strict punishment system for kitchen staff who make cooking errors
options.B: A continuous process of gathering feedback and adjusting meals to meet client needs
options.C: A one-time inspection that happens only when the kitchen first opens
options.D: A method to permanently stop changing the food served in the ward

explanation: It's all about checking in regularly, listening to patient feedback, and tweaking the menu so everyone is well-fed and happy. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h7)

question: What happens to a gland's tissue when it experiences ischemia or infarction?

options.A: Cells multiply uncontrollably to produce more hormones
options.B: The gland enlarges rapidly due to excess fluid
options.C: It temporarily stops working but recovers on its own
options.D: Tissue dies because it lacks adequate blood supply

explanation: Ischemia means blood flow is cut off. If those cells are starved of oxygen and nutrients for too long, they sadly die (infarction). [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do misplaced endometrial implants cause ongoing pain and scarring in the pelvis?

options.A: They grow rapidly into malignant tumors within weeks
options.B: They release massive amounts of male hormones into the abdomen
options.C: They bleed during each cycle, causing local inflammation and adhesions
options.D: They destroy the nerves supplying the lower abdominal wall

explanation: Wherever these misplaced cells land, they still respond to monthly hormones by trying to 'bleed'. This trapped blood irritates nearby tissue, causing painful inflammation and sticky scar tissue. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h6)

question: Why is protein intake typically increased alongside total calories in stressed clinical states?

options.A: To stimulate the production of red blood cells
options.B: To serve as the primary source of quick cellular energy
options.C: To rebuild damaged tissue and prevent muscle wasting
options.D: To slow down gastrointestinal motility

explanation: Proteins supply the essential building blocks needed to repair wounds and maintain lean body mass during hypermetabolic illness. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h3)

question: A community action plan includes assigning specific tasks to local youth groups. What is the main benefit of this?

options.A: It guarantees that international donors will send more money
options.B: It builds local capacity and ensures project sustainability
options.C: It eliminates the need for any monitoring or supervision
options.D: It prevents the nurses from doing any actual field work

explanation: Involving local groups builds their skills and ensures the community can maintain the health interventions long after external nurses leave. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: What causes the stiffness of rigor mortis after a person passes away?

options.A: An excessive buildup of acetylcholine in the neuromuscular junction
options.B: Continuous nerve signals firing from the brain
options.C: A lack of ATP preventing myosin heads from detaching from actin
options.D: The permanent destruction of troponin within the sarcomere

explanation: Without cellular energy (ATP) to act as the release button, muscles can't let go. They stay locked in place, causing that classic post-mortem stiffness. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h6)

question: A tele-nurse sees that a heart failure patient's daily weight readings are steadily climbing. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Contact the patient to assess for worsening fluid overload symptoms
options.B: Ignore the data until the patient's next scheduled annual checkup
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Delete the readings because home devices are always inaccurate

explanation: Quick thinking! Gaining weight fast in heart failure often means the body is holding onto extra fluid. Calling the patient lets you catch it early before they end up in the hospital. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h3)

question: A patient with breast cancer and bone metastases is drowsy, confused, and very weak. Which metabolic emergency is most likely occurring?

options.A: Hyponatremia
options.B: Tumor Lysis Syndrome
options.C: Hypercalcemia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Tumors affecting the bones release excess calcium into the blood, causing neurological dullness, muscle weakness, and profound fatigue. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h2)

question: Where are emergency and trauma operating suites usually placed in a hospital layout?

options.A: In a separate building far from the main wards
options.B: On the top floor near the administrative offices
options.C: Close to the emergency department for fast access
options.D: Next to the hospital laundry and kitchen facilities

explanation: Spot on! When a patient is bleeding out from a trauma, every single second counts, so being right next to the emergency department is a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a major duty of a registered dietitian in a hospital?

options.A: Administering routine intravenous medications to patients
options.B: Prescribing medical nutrition therapy and assessing status
options.C: Ordering all diagnostic blood tests for the ward
options.D: Performing surgical procedures on the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: Exactly! Dietitians are the experts at evaluating a patient's nutritional health and designing specific therapeutic diets for recovery. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h3)

question: What is the best way for a patient to manage mild dry mouth caused by an anti-spasmodic medication?

options.A: Take small, frequent sips of water or chew sugarless gum
options.B: Take a strong diuretic pill to balance out body fluids
options.C: Stop the medication completely without telling the doctor
options.D: Apply medicated eye drops into the oral cavity

explanation: Simple tricks like sipping water or chewing sugar-free gum help keep the mouth moist and comfortable without ruining their treatment plan. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why should nurses avoid relying solely on a patient's verbal report about taking their medications?

options.A: Patients often claim they take pills even when they miss them
options.B: Patients never remember the names of their prescribed drugs
options.C: Verbal reports are illegal to record in hospital charts
options.D: Doctors prefer laboratory tests over talking to patients

explanation: Patients want to please their healthcare providers and often say they take their medications faithfully when they actually do not. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is it so important to keep protein intake up while on a low-calorie diet?

options.A: To speed up quick water retention
options.B: To preserve lean muscle mass
options.C: To stop normal kidney filtration
options.D: To block all carbohydrate digestion

explanation: Well done! Eating enough protein gives your body the building blocks it needs so it burns fat instead of breaking down your hard-earned muscle. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T010#GNS227_U6_T010_h3)

question: A clinic expects to use 2,000 syringes during a vaccination drive. If each safety box holds 100 syringes, how many safety boxes are required?
explanation: Divide the total number of used syringes (2,000) by the capacity of a single box (100), which equals 20 boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why are faith-based health clinics so important in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: They possess unlimited budgets from foreign governments
options.B: They charge the highest fees for specialized surgeries
options.C: They frequently establish hospitals in remote and underserved areas
options.D: They focus exclusively on urban corporate executives

explanation: Faith-based groups have a long history of setting up clinics in rural or hard-to-reach places where government hospitals might not have reached yet. [learn more](GST322_U5_T3#GST322_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a biological factor that affects emotional health?

options.A: Monthly income and housing stability
options.B: Access to community parks and recreation
options.C: Cultural beliefs about mental illness
options.D: Genetic predispositions and neurochemistry

explanation: Biological factors are all about what's happening inside our bodies—like our genes, physical health, and brain chemistry. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary outcome of mitosis in somatic cells?

options.A: Two identical daughter cells
options.B: Four unique gamete cells
options.C: Two haploid sex cells
options.D: One large multinucleated cell

explanation: Mitosis duplicates a somatic cell's genetic material and divides it to create two genetically identical cells for growth and repair. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h5)

question: How are health outcomes usually measured in a Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: Natural clinical units like life-years gained or blood pressure lowered
options.B: Subjective happiness scales completely unrelated to physical health
options.C: Monetary amounts such as dollars or naira earned by the hospital
options.D: Total number of staff employed in the outpatient department

explanation: Instead of money, cost-effectiveness looks at real clinical results—like millimeters of mercury dropped in blood pressure or extra years of life gained. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h4)

question: What does it mean when a patient's emotional distress is described as 'somaticized'?

options.A: Seeking immediate help from a specialized psychiatrist
options.B: Denying that any mental or physical health problem exists
options.C: Isolating oneself from family and friends during a crisis
options.D: Expressing emotional pain entirely through physical bodily complaints

explanation: Think of somaticization as the body speaking what the heart cannot. It's when emotional pain turns into very real physical signs like headaches, stomach aches, or crushing fatigue. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why do quality improvement experts focus on fixing systems instead of blaming individual nurses when mistakes happen?

options.A: Because clinical systems are structured to produce the exact results they currently deliver
options.B: Because hospital management lacks the authority to discipline workers
options.C: Because individual staff members never make mistakes during busy shifts
options.D: Because nurses are legally protected from facing disciplinary action in hospitals

explanation: When workflows are confusing or rushed, mistakes are bound to happen. Fixing the system helps everyone succeed, rather than pointing fingers at the nurse! [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do many Nigerian patients choose private health facilities even though they must pay cash out of pocket?

options.A: They often perceive private care to have better quality and shorter waiting times
options.B: Private hospitals offer free medications to every registered citizen
options.C: Private clinics are entirely subsidized by federal government revenue
options.D: The law forbids them from visiting public hospitals for minor illnesses

explanation: Frustration with long queues and drug stockouts in public hospitals drives many citizens to private clinics, cost notwithstanding. It's a clear indicator of systemic challenges! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h6)

question: A patient with heart failure suddenly feels short of breath. Which nursing action should you take first regarding their position?

options.A: Place the patient face down in the prone position
options.B: Elevate the head of the bed to semi-Fowler's
options.C: Tilt the bed head downward into Trendelenburg
options.D: Lay the patient completely flat in the supine position

explanation: Sitting them up in semi-Fowler's makes breathing so much easier by taking pressure off their lungs and heart. Great job! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) is released by almost all autonomic preganglionic nerve fibers?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Norepinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the go-to chemical messenger used at the first synapse (ganglion) for both the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions. Great job! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why can no single agency handle a major disaster completely on its own?

options.A: Government rules forbid any agency from working alone
options.B: Agencies prefer to wait for outside help before starting
options.C: Individual organizations lack any trained leadership staff
options.D: No single agency has all the necessary resources and expertise

explanation: Major emergencies overwhelm the capacity of any single group, making teamwork across various sectors necessary for survival and recovery. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why does a birth attendant massage the mother's uterus gently after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: To help the mother expel remaining amniotic fluid
options.B: To encourage uterine contraction and prevent heavy bleeding
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the breasts
options.D: To reposition the internal organs properly

explanation: Uterine massage compresses open blood vessels at the placental site, which is the primary defense against postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h6)

question: How do acquired bleeding problems differ from inherited conditions like hemophilia?

options.A: Acquired disorders develop later in life due to illnesses or deficiencies
options.B: Inherited disorders only show up during major surgery in adulthood
options.C: Inherited disorders can be cured easily with simple vitamin supplements
options.D: Acquired disorders only affect red blood cells instead of platelets

explanation: While inherited conditions are passed down in your genes from birth, acquired disorders pop up later in life because of illness, poor nutrition, or certain medications. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T11#GNS311_U2_T11_h1)

question: When should a nurse collect a wound culture specimen in relation to starting antibiotics?

options.A: At the exact same time as the first dose
options.B: Only after the patient develops a fever
options.C: Before starting the antibiotics
options.D: Three days after finishing the antibiotics

explanation: Always swab or collect cultures *before* giving antibiotics! If you start the drugs first, they'll kill the germs in the sample and you won't find out what's causing the infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h9)

question: What is the main natural job of saliva inside our mouths?

options.A: Gluing loose teeth tightly back into the jawbone
options.B: Killing off every fungus that enters through the throat
options.C: Washing away food bits and fighting off harmful acids
options.D: Bleaching tooth enamel to keep teeth sparkling white

explanation: Think of saliva as your mouth's built-in cleaning crew! It constantly washes away debris and neutralizes acids to keep your teeth safe. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h2)

question: Who is considered a vital stakeholder in a nursing quality improvement project?

options.A: External auditors from the tax office
options.B: Only the hospital chief executive officer
options.C: Private security guards at the hospital gate
options.D: Frontline nurses, physicians, and patients

explanation: Spot on! Successful healthcare relies on teamwork. Everyone involved in giving or receiving care needs a seat at the table. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h5)

question: A patient with a bacterial infection wants to stop taking antibiotics after two days because they feel fine. What should you tell them?

options.A: They must double the remaining dose on the third day instead
options.B: They should save the remaining pills for a headache next week
options.C: Stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and more resistant
options.D: It is completely safe to stop once fever symptoms disappear

explanation: You got it! Always encourage patients to finish the full dose so the infection doesn't bounce back stronger. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why do problems in the brain-testicle hormone pathway (hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis) often affect both sperm and testosterone?

options.A: Because the pituitary gland directly manufactures all male gametes
options.B: Because hypothalamic neurons physically transform into mature spermatozoa
options.C: Because testosterone is exclusively stored in the anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Because the axis controls both testosterone production and germ cell maturation

explanation: Think of the brain as the master switch that controls two main factories: Leydig cells for testosterone and Sertoli cells for sperm. When the master switch has issues, both processes are affected! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h1)

question: How is disaster triage different from regular emergency department triage?

options.A: Routine triage is only used when there are zero available beds
options.B: Disaster triage focuses on saving the greatest number with limited resources
options.C: Routine triage ignores vital signs while disaster triage requires full lab work

question: Why is learning about infectious agents so important for a community health nurse?

question: How do you usually check the baby's heartbeat during a normal home birth?

question: Which of these counts as pathological waste?

question: What dangerous gases or chemicals are released when medical plastics and waste are burned in open drums?

question: How do major adverse events mostly hurt a healthcare facility financially?

options.D: Through lawsuits, fines, and extended patient stays

question: Why are hospitals moving from paper ledgers to digital health records?

question: Why is it important to use local imagery and familiar faces in health education illustrations?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective cross-sector collaboration?

question: You are wrapping up an admission chat with a new patient. Which action belongs to the termination phase?

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey?

question: Which sign is a classic warning of even mild dehydration in older adults?

question: In a busy clinic with limited resources, what is one of the best ways to reduce airborne germ spread?

question: Why do event planners use zigzag or serpentine queues at entrance gates?

options.C: To comply with indoor plumbing regulations

question: During a follow-up assessment, what must a nurse always screen for directly?

question: What is existential distress primarily centered around?

question: What kind of tumor grows into nearby tissues and travels to other parts of the body?

question: As a student nurse, why should you avoid shaking dirty bed linen in the air?

question: Why can't hospitals quickly increase their supply of healthcare services during a sudden disease outbreak?

options.C: Hospitals operate with an endless surplus of fully qualified nursing staff

question: What is the best first step for a unit manager when an unexpected error happens on the ward?

question: What is the primary goal of healthcare risk management?

question: Which popular local dietary combination is most famous for triggering painful gout attacks?

question: During which procedure is the lithotomy position most commonly used?

question: Why are long-acting injectable (LAI) medications often preferred for patients on psychiatric parole?

question: Why do intestinal cells have to package dietary fats into structures called chylomicrons?

question: What serious condition is strongly suspected when you see severe, locked Grade 3 moulding during labour?

question: What is a common cultural barrier that stops some communities from accepting routine immunization?

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is most known for triggering dangerous heart rhythm changes?

options.A: Bicarbonate

question: Which complication should a nurse watch for most closely right after a hysterectomy?

question: Why does the body increase blood volume so massively during pregnancy?

question: A nurse manager needs to buy daily supplies of syringes and gauze. Under which budget category do these routine expenses fall?

question: A family member stops going to work to care for a sick relative. What type of cost is this?

question: What is the primary basis for sorting patients at emergency triage?

question: Why must nurses shift their focus from curing to optimizing health when caring for patients with permanent physical disabilities?

question: What is the main focus of community nutrition compared to hospital dietetics?

question: What is the main goal of using an explanatory research design in nursing?

question: What is the main goal of contact tracing when an infectious disease breaks out?

question: During which step of the planning process does a nurse manager weigh the pros and cons of different staffing methods?

question: What usually takes up the biggest chunk of a hospital's daily budget?

question: How does community health nursing mainly differ from taking care of patients at the bedside?

question: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), what age range covers adolescents and youths?

question: What is a major purpose of conducting performance appraisals for nurses?

question: Why do nurses check out the living space during a home health visit?

question: A mother denies her toddler eggs due to a local belief. What is the biggest danger of this practice?

question: Why is using digital health records often better than old-fashioned paper notes?

question: What is a key duty of healthcare leaders when it comes to safety culture?

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in the hospital?

question: A patient's mother-in-law says she shouldn't eat eggs or the baby will be born hairless. How should you, as the nurse, respond?

question: Which chart is commonly used in the clinic to test a patient's eyesight?

question: What is the main goal of Maternal and Child Health (MCH) services?

question: What should a nurse manager focus on during a disciplinary interview?

question: What kind of nursing assessment should you perform to uncover a patient's environmental risk factors?

question: What is a big benefit of linking smart bed scales directly to the Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

question: A patient with a known femur tumor suddenly cries out in severe pain after rolling over in bed and can no longer bear weight. What likely happened?

question: After a very tough shift, which activity helps a nurse process their emotions and learn from the experience?

options.C: Changing clinical wards
options.D: Filing an incident report

explanation: Writing down your thoughts in a reflective journal is a great way to unwind, process tough moments, and grow into a stronger nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h8)

question: How can nursing management figure out if communication between departments is breaking down?

options.A: Analyzing incident reports related to handoff failures

options.C: Checking the personal social media accounts of staff
options.D: Counting the number of beds in storage

explanation: Spot on! Incident reports show managers exactly where handoffs went wrong, helping them fix those problem areas. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h7)

question: Which body feature makes female patients more likely to get a catheter-related urinary tract infection?

options.D: A shorter urethra close to the anal opening

question: You need to help move a heavy patient up in bed. Which of these follows safe ergonomic practices?

options.A: Holding the patient far away from the body to keep uniform clean
options.B: Bending sharply at the waist with straight knees to gain momentum
options.C: Twisting the torso quickly while lifting to reach the bedside table
options.D: Using a mechanical lift or asking a colleague for assistance

explanation: Never try to be a lone hero with heavy lifting! Always ask a colleague to team-lift or use mechanical aids to protect your lower back. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h5)

question: In immunology, what exactly is an antigen?

options.A: A medication used to lower systemic inflammation
options.B: A foreign substance that triggers an immune response
options.C: A physical barrier found in human skin layers
options.D: A white blood cell that produces Y-shaped proteins
