question: Which strategy is most effective when educating rural community members about pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: Using simple local dialects and relatable community gathering spaces
options.B: Hosting lectures exclusively in urban tertiary teaching hospitals
options.C: Requiring written exams before women can attend antenatal care
options.D: Distributing dense medical journals written in advanced technical terms

explanation: Effective community health education meets people where they are, using familiar language and local venues like markets or places of worship. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h5)

question: What is a very common emotional reaction for a nurse who is caught up in the second victim phenomenon?

options.A: Immediate anger directed exclusively at the hospital management
options.B: Complete emotional numbness with zero memory of the event
options.C: Intense guilt and self-doubt regarding clinical skills
options.D: A sense of relief that the error was finally discovered

explanation: It's heartbreakingly common to question your abilities after a mistake. Remember, making an error doesn't mean you're a bad nurse—it makes you human. Be kind to yourself! [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why do healthcare workers worry so much about carbapenem-resistant germs?

options.A: Powerful last-resort drugs for severe infections
options.B: Over-the-counter supplements for viral colds
options.C: Mild topical ointments for minor skin rashes
options.D: Preventative vaccines given during childhood

explanation: Carbapenems are our heavy-duty antibiotics. When germs resist them, we are left with very few options in the treatment bag! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h4)

question: What is the main use of tally sheets during a busy immunization outreach?

options.A: To serve as the child's permanent health card kept at home
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of running the clinic
options.C: To quickly record each dose given using tick marks without slowing down
options.D: To track the exact temperature of the vaccine carrier

explanation: Tally sheets are a nurse's best friend in a busy crowd—just quick tick marks to keep an accurate count while saving time! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h7)

question: What important safety advice should a nurse give a patient about stopping anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Stop taking them right away if your mouth feels dry
options.B: Reduce the dose slowly as advised by your doctor
options.C: Crush all the tablets so they clear your system faster
options.D: Double the dose if your tremors start coming back

explanation: You've got it! Stopping these meds suddenly can cause rebound muscle stiffness and make tremors flare up fiercely. Always taper safely! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

options.A: To store mature sperm cells
options.B: To produce alkaline seminal fluid
options.C: To secrete testosterone
options.D: To nourish the urinary bladder

explanation: Leydig cells live right between the sperm-producing tubes and act as the main factories for pumping out testosterone in the male body. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand national economic factors?

options.A: Financial factors have no bearing on daily clinical nursing practice.
options.B: Nurses are solely responsible for setting national taxation rates.
options.C: Economic stress directly impacts a patient's ability to manage their health.
options.D: Understanding economics allows nurses to set hospital drug prices.

explanation: Poverty and financial instability influence whether a patient can afford medications, follow proper nutrition, or access care when needed. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of descriptive statistics in a study?

options.A: Summarize the basic features and scores of the sample data
options.B: Replace the need for taking patient medical histories
options.C: Prove that a new drug cures a disease in all humans
options.D: Determine the financial cost of running a hospital ward

explanation: Descriptive statistics give you a quick, clear snapshot of what your sample looks like using simple summaries like averages and percentages. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h4)

question: What does the intrapleural route of medication administration involve?

options.A: Administering fluids through a large vein in the chest
options.B: Injecting drugs straight into the main lung tissue
options.C: Delivering medication directly into the pleural space
options.D: Giving oral pills that target respiratory infections

explanation: You've got this! The intrapleural route simply means putting the medicine right into that thin space surrounding the lungs, rather than giving it by mouth or through a regular vein. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T12#GNS125_U3_T12_h1)

question: What usually happens shortly after a care-seeking patient gets normal test results from a doctor?

options.A: The anxiety returns and doubt creeps back in
options.B: The patient is permanently cured of all health fears
options.C: The patient stops visiting hospitals for the rest of life
options.D: The patient develops severe physical paralysis

explanation: Medical reassurance rarely lasts long for them. Soon enough, doubt creeps back in, and they start questioning if the lab results were a mistake. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h4)

question: What popular model explains that errors happen when multiple system defenses fail all at once?

options.A: The SBAR communication chain
options.B: The Swiss cheese model
options.C: The root cause hierarchy
options.D: The Just Culture pyramid

explanation: You got it! Think of safety layers like slices of Swiss cheese. Accidents only happen when the holes in every single slice line up at the same time. [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is an example of a non-clinical outsourced hospital service?

options.A: Administering intravenous medications
options.B: Hospital laundry and facility maintenance
options.C: Specialized renal dialysis procedures
options.D: Diagnostic laboratory blood testing

explanation: Things like cleaning, washing linens, and security are support services that don't involve direct medical treatment, making them great for outsourcing. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h5)

question: A pregnant woman in a low-income community skips her antenatal visits to buy food for her children. What economic factor is primarily driving her decision?

options.A: Macroeconomic surplus
options.B: Out-of-pocket financial barrier
options.C: Brain drain
options.D: Excess health insurance coverage

explanation: Having to choose between basic survival needs like food and paying for medical care highlights the harsh impact of direct out-of-pocket expenses. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h5)

question: What major environmental problem is caused by poorly operated, low-temperature medical incinerators?

options.A: Complete disappearance of municipal electricity grids
options.B: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the air
options.C: Immediate flooding of nearby hospital wards
options.D: Excessive production of harmless oxygen gas

explanation: Burning medical waste at low temperatures without proper filters releases nasty chemical pollutants like dioxins and furans into our air. High standards matter! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: Why must community health nurses work closely with WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) teams in an IDP camp?

options.A: Clean water and proper sanitation directly prevent waterborne infectious diseases
options.B: Sanitation workers handle the psychiatric evaluation of adults
options.C: Nurses need assistance with ordering hospital furniture
options.D: WASH engineers are responsible for diagnosing clinical malaria

explanation: Good health in a camp relies heavily on clean water and toilets, making teamwork between nurses and WASH teams a must. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T20#GNS225_U5_T20_h6)

question: Which specific cells inside the testes make testosterone?

options.A: Leydig cells
options.B: Germ cells
options.C: Sertoli cells
options.D: Brunner cells

explanation: Leydig cells are the hardworking factories inside the testes that pump out testosterone whenever they get the signal from the brain! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h2)

question: A doctor prescribes a brand name drug for a patient, but the hospital dispenses the generic equivalent. What is the most appropriate action for the nurse?

options.A: Administer the medication, knowing the active ingredient is identical
options.B: Discard the medication because generic drugs cannot be substituted safely
options.C: Call the doctor to report that the pharmacy gave an unauthorized fake drug
options.D: Refuse to give the drug until the brand name version is brought from home

explanation: As long as the active ingredient and strength match, the generic drug is therapeutically equivalent and totally safe to give your patient. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h6)

question: During a mass casualty incident, you check a patient with a massive head injury who has no pulse and isn't breathing. What triage tag do they get?

options.A: Black
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Red
options.D: Green

explanation: Correct! A black tag is used for the deceased or for patients whose injuries are so severe that available resources cannot save them. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does community stigma often affect families living with an HIV-positive member?

options.A: It forces local health clinics to provide free housing
options.B: It causes families to isolate themselves from others
options.C: It encourages families to seek out more social groups
options.D: It improves the family's financial stability over time

explanation: Exactly. Fear of unfair judgment and discrimination can make households withdraw from friends and community activities out of worry. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h2)

question: Which finding around a skeletal traction pin site means you need to call the doctor right away?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crust around the metal entry point

options.C: Mild skin redness close to the pin

question: How many milligrams are in a single gram?

options.D: 1,000,000 milligrams

question: Which of these is generally safe and does NOT harm sperm production?

options.D: Exposure to heavy toxins

explanation: Good news! Regular, moderate exercise keeps your body healthy and balanced. Heat, harsh toxins, and steroids, however, can hurt sperm counts. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T6#GNS121_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why do many patients in Nigeria often report body tiredness rather than emotional feelings?

options.C: Physical illness is the only recognized health issue in the region

question: Who is considered a 'susceptible host'?

options.A: A patient who has complete immunity against all infections
options.B: An individual whose immune system cannot resist an invading pathogen
options.C: A person who currently carries a germ without symptoms
options.D: An object or surface where bacteria live and multiply

explanation: Right on! A susceptible host is simply someone whose body defense is low enough for germs to easily move in and cause sickness. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is an essential post-procedure nursing check after an EPS?

options.A: Checking deep tendon reflexes in both upper arms

options.C: Checking pulses and color in the extremity used for catheter insertion

question: What is the main purpose of defining a 'case' during an outbreak investigation?

question: Which of these counts as skilled nursing care at home?

question: A lab report shows normal skin bacteria growing in a urine sample that was collected carelessly. What is this called?

options.A: Contamination

question: What is spermatogenesis?

options.B: The storage of mature sperm inside the epididymis

question: Why is educating community and religious leaders an effective way to fight child trafficking?

options.A: They possess the legal power to arrest and prosecute criminals
options.B: They provide free medical treatment to all trafficking victims
options.C: They fund all government anti-trafficking agencies
options.D: They can help monitor for suspicious strangers and false agents

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the rinse water always flow?

question: A patient asks how Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) works. How should you explain it?

question: How do bacteria usually share drug resistance traits with each other so quickly?

question: When should a nurse refer a postpartum mother to a specialized family planning clinic?

question: How do nurses best create a supportive clinical environment for FGM survivors?

question: Why do males use the same tube (the urethra) for both urine and semen?

question: What is the chemical neurotransmitter released at the neuromuscular junction?

question: What is the primary goal of nursing care during a psychiatric or behavioral emergency?

options.A: Proving the patient is at fault for their behavior
options.B: Immediately discharging the patient to home
options.C: Starting long-term psychotherapy in the emergency bay
options.D: Ensuring safety and de-escalating the crisis

explanation: Keeping everyone safe and calming the patient down is always your first priority in any mental health emergency. You've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do we actually need dietary fats to absorb certain vitamins?

options.A: Fat binds directly to water-soluble vitamins
options.B: Fat makes the stomach produce more acid
options.C: Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fat
options.D: Fat stops the liver from destroying vitamins

explanation: Think of fat as the vehicle that carries vitamins A, D, E, and K through your gut so your body can use them. Without fat, these vitamins just pass right through! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h1)

question: Why should a nurse ask non-judgmental questions when assessing a patient's medication habits?

options.A: To trick the patient into admitting they forgot their appointments
options.B: To avoid having to check the pharmacy refill records
options.C: To ensure the doctor prescribes stronger antibiotics next time
options.D: To encourage the patient to speak honestly without fear of scolding

explanation: Patients often lie about missing doses out of fear of being reprimanded by healthcare workers. A warm, non-judgmental approach builds trust and uncovers the truth. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h4)

question: What type of molecule usually acts as a T-dependent antigen?

options.A: Water molecules
options.B: Plain lipids

question: Why is it dangerous to just silence an infusion pump alarm and walk away?

options.A: Unresolved alarms cause the pump to reverse fluid flow into the bag
options.B: It can delay necessary treatment or fail to catch a dangerous blockage
options.C: Hospital policy fines staff members who touch alarms too quickly

explanation: You got it! Alarms are there for a reason. Ignoring them without fixing the root cause can leave your patient without their meds or miss a serious line problem. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h6)

question: What defines a faith-based organization in the health sector?

options.C: It receives all its funding directly from the federal tax board
options.D: It only treats patients who share a specific political view

question: What complication can happen if large amounts of plain tap water are used for lavage in young children?

options.C: Sudden spikes in blood pressure throughout the body

question: If a researcher labels 'Male' as 1 and 'Female' as 2 in a survey, what is this step called?

options.C: Hypothesis testing
options.D: Cleaning

question: A nurse forgets to check a client's IV infusion site, leading to severe tissue swelling and necrosis. Which element of malpractice is demonstrated by the tissue damage?

options.A: Duty of care
options.B: Professional immunity
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Actual damages

explanation: The physical tissue injury and necrosis represent the actual harm or damages suffered by the client due to poor care. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h7)

question: What does the principle of unity of command mean in nursing?

options.A: All nurses must wear the exact same uniform
options.B: The head nurse makes all clinical decisions alone
options.C: Every shift must start at the exact same hour
options.D: Each nurse reports to only one direct supervisor

explanation: Unity of command prevents confusion by ensuring an employee receives orders from and is accountable to a single boss. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h2)

question: When would you use an independent samples t-test?

options.A: When comparing two completely separate groups of people
options.B: When there is no control group in the study
options.C: When analyzing categorical data with three or more groups
options.D: When measuring the same patients twice over time

question: What does the principle of equity mean in community mobilisation?

options.A: Treating only the village elders during an outbreak
options.B: Fair distribution of health benefits without discrimination
options.C: Building clinics only in big cities
options.D: Giving equal amounts of money to every single adult

question: A patient asks how long an egg can survive and be fertilized after ovulation. What is your best response?

options.B: About 24 hours
options.C: Less than 1 hour
options.D: Exactly 1 week

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of fake nutrition advice?

options.A: Advising patients to eat a balanced variety of all food groups
options.B: Publishing raw data from randomized and controlled clinical trials
options.C: Requiring regular blood tests supervised by a registered dietitian
options.D: Promising a single product can cure many different diseases

explanation: If one simple tea or supplement claims to cure everything from malaria to headaches, run the other way! Real medicine doesn't work that way. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h3)

question: Why do we call vitamins and minerals 'micronutrients'?

options.A: They do not play any significant role in overall human metabolism
options.B: They are required by the body in much smaller quantities than macronutrients
options.C: They can only be manufactured synthetically inside a laboratory
options.D: They contain fewer chemical atoms than proteins and fats

explanation: Think 'micro' for tiny amounts! Even though we only need them in small quantities, they are still super important for our health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h2)

question: How should your team view a test of change that doesn't work out as planned?

options.B: As a personal failure of the nursing supervisor on duty
options.C: As proof that quality improvement initiatives never work
options.D: As useful learning data that highlights workflow barriers

question: What is the medical term for fluid building up inside the belly (peritoneal cavity)?

question: What would happen to the accessory sex glands if a man's testosterone levels dropped very low?

options.A: They would shrink and decrease their secretions
options.B: They would grow larger and produce excess fluid
options.C: They would immediately start producing female hormones
options.D: They would convert into urinary storage tissues

question: Why is it important to honestly tell patients and families when a medical error happens?

options.C: It speeds up the physical healing process of the injured patient
options.D: It builds trust and fulfills the ethical obligation of transparency

explanation: Well done! Honesty is always the best policy in nursing. Telling the truth when mistakes happen builds real trust between patients, families, and the healthcare team. [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which type of medication is given to treat intestinal worm infections?

options.A: Antihypertensives
options.B: Anthelmintics
options.C: Antivirals
options.D: Antifungals

explanation: Think 'anti' (against) and 'helmintic' (worms)! Anthelmintics are the specific drugs nurses administer to clear out parasitic worms. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h5)

question: How should the normal esophagus appear on a healthy barium swallow image?

options.A: A wide pouch with multiple jagged blockages
options.B: A rigid, non-moving tube with thickened walls
options.C: A smooth, straight tubular structure with uniform width
options.D: A completely closed channel with zero contrast entry

explanation: A healthy esophagus shows an even, smooth column of barium moving down without unusual narrowing, widening, or pouching. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h5)

question: You just finished giving an injection. What should you do immediately with the used syringe and needle?

options.A: Remove the needle carefully with bare fingers and throw it in the dustbin
options.B: Drop the entire unit straight into the puncture-proof sharps container
options.C: Place the needle on the bedside table until the end of the shift
options.D: Break the needle in half to save space inside the disposal box

explanation: Drop the whole un-recapped syringe and needle right into your safety box. No taking parts apart, no bending—just straight in! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h7)

question: How do we calculate the pentavalent dropout rate at a primary health clinic?

options.A: Comparing measles vaccine uptake with the number of newborn babies
options.B: Subtracting total children immunized from the total birth population
options.C: Comparing pentavalent dose 1 numbers with pentavalent dose 3 numbers
options.D: Dividing total vaccine doses administered by the number of clinic days

explanation: We find the dropout rate by comparing how many babies took the first dose versus how many actually made it back for the third dose. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h5)

question: What is the main internal chip that powers a microcomputer?

options.A: A massive cooling tower
options.B: A microprocessor
options.C: A dual mainframe processor
options.D: An analog wave converter

question: A student nurse uses her password to log into the EMR and opens the chart of a famous musician on another floor just out of curiosity. What has happened here?

options.A: A helpful act of teamwork to see if the patient needs extra visitors
options.B: A routine computer system update performed by the IT department
options.C: An unauthorized privacy breach that can be tracked by audit software
options.D: Standard nursing practice for checking hospital bed occupancy rates

question: What do Lewy bodies do inside the brain cells of someone with Parkinson's disease?

options.A: They protect neurons from inflammatory damage in the midbrain.
options.B: They accumulate inside nerve cells and disrupt normal cellular function.
options.C: They produce excessive amounts of dopamine to compensate for cell loss.
options.D: They repair damaged myelin sheaths around peripheral nerves.

explanation: Think of Lewy bodies like unwanted trash piling up inside the cell. These abnormal protein clumps build up, causing the nerve cells to get damaged and eventually die off. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the biggest danger of pouring leftover chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.D: The plastic material dissolves within a few hours

question: What is the main goal of having a "just culture" in a hospital?

options.A: Allowing senior doctors to break hospital rules without consequences
options.B: Ensuring that every single staff member receives the exact same salary
options.C: Punishing every nurse immediately when a minor paperwork error happens
options.D: Encouraging staff to report mistakes openly without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: Spot on! When nurses and staff feel safe speaking up about errors, the whole hospital becomes safer for everyone. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)
